correctness.rationale: Invariant symmetrization preserves mass and Fourier positivity; Fourier Krawtchouk expansion is exact and normalized. The polynomial with zeros at consecutive integer weights is feasible because of integer-grid positivity. The dual identity with explicitly nonnegative alpha and beta bounds every feasible polynomial and gives the complete radial equality analysis. Exact tests: 558 rational cases and six full Fourier transforms passed; the infinite theorem uses the algebraic proof, not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The exact all-alphabet, all-dimension positive-definite Turan invariant of a canonical Hamming metric ball solves a natural harmonic extremal problem, not an arbitrary numerical slice. The sharp congruence transition from one radial optimizer to a line segment and fractional mass values such as 27/2 for q=3,d=5 are motivated structural facts. A Fourier dual certificate is reusable in coding and packing contexts without claiming new code bounds.
